passages.heading: MD&A
passages.text: OVERVIEW AT&T Inc. is referred to as “we,” “AT&T” or the “Company” throughout this document. AT&T products and services are provided or offered by subsidiaries and affiliates of AT&T Inc. under the AT&T brand and not by AT&T Inc., and the names of the particular subsidiaries and affiliates providing the services generally have been omitted. AT&T is a holding company whose subsidiaries and affiliates operate worldwide in the telecommunications and technology industries. You should read this discussion in conjunction with the consolidated financial statements and accompanying notes (Notes). Our Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations included in this document generally discusses 2025 and 2024 items and year-to-year comparisons between 2025 and 2024. Discussions of 2023 items and year-to-year comparisons between 2024 and 2023 that are not included in this document can be found in “Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations” in Part II, Item 7 of our Annual Report on Form 10 ‑ K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2024. We have two reportable segments: Communications and Latin America. Our segment results presented in Note 4 and discussed below follow our internal management reporting. Each segment’s percentage calculation of total segment operating revenue is derived from our segment results table in Note 4. Segment operating income is primarily attributable to our Communications segment due to prior-years operating losses in Latin America. passages.heading: Risk factors
passages.text: In addition to the other information set forth in this document, including the matters contained under the heading “Cautionary Language Concerning Forward-Looking Statements,” you should carefully read the matters described below. We believe that each of these matters could materially affect our business. Most, if not all, of these factors are beyond our ability to control. Macro-Economic Factors: Adverse changes in the U.S. securities markets, a higher interest rate environment, rising inflation and medical costs could materially increase our benefit plan costs and future funding requirements. Our costs to provide current benefits and funding for future benefits are subject to increases, primarily due to continuing increases in medical and prescription drug costs, in part due to inflation, and can be affected by lower returns on assets held by our pension and other benefit plans, which are reflected in our financial statements for that year. In calculating the recognized benefit costs, we have made certain assumptions regarding future investment returns, interest rates and medical costs. These assumptions could change significantly over time and could be materially different than originally projected. Lower than assumed investment returns, an increase in our benefit obligations, and higher than assumed medical and prescription drug costs will increase expenses. The Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB) requires companies to recognize the funded status of defined benefit pension and postretirement plans as an asset or liability in their statement of financial position and to recognize changes in that funded status in the year in which the changes occur. We have elected to reflect the annual adjustments to the funded status in our consolidated statement of income. Therefore, an increase in our costs or adverse market conditions will have a negative effect on our operating results. Significant adverse changes in capital markets could result in the deterioration of our defined benefit plans’ funded status. Inflationary pressures on costs, such as inputs for devices we sell and network components, labor and distribution costs, may impact our network construction, our financial condition or results of operations. As a provider of telecommunications and technology services, we sell handsets, wireless data cards, wireless computing devices and customer premises equipment manufactured by various suppliers for use with our voice and data services and depend on suppliers to provide us, directly or through other suppliers, with items such as network equipment, customer premises equipment, and wireless-related equipment such as mobile hotspots, handsets, wirelessly enabled computers, wireless data cards and other connected devices for our customers. In recent years, the costs of these inputs and the costs of labor necessary to develop, deploy and maintain our networks and our products and services have increased. credit_strengths.text: AT&T's operating cash flow comfortably covers capital expenditure, leaving substantial free cash flow that supports debt service and shareholder returns. The company's scale in wireless and fiber underpins recurring revenue and stable cash generation, with operating cash flow trending upward over the past three years.

Operating income has recovered strongly, driving interest coverage above the sector median and providing a solid cushion against earnings volatility. The Communications segment, which accounts for nearly all segment operating income, benefits from integrated product offerings and shared network assets.

key_risks.text: AT&T's debt maturity profile is heavily weighted to later years, but the company still faces meaningful refinancing needs in the near term. With a substantial portion of debt maturing beyond year five, refinancing risk is concentrated in future periods, exposing the company to interest rate movements and market conditions.

Inflationary pressures on network components, labor, and device costs could compress margins and cash flow, while rising medical and pension costs may increase benefit obligations. These cost pressures, combined with a higher interest rate environment, could strain profitability and debt servicing capacity.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Interest coverage is adequate but below the sector median, indicating less headroom relative to peers. Free cash flow to debt is modest, and while operating cash flow is strong, the company's ability to service debt depends on sustaining current earnings levels amid competitive and cost pressures.

Net leverage sits above the sector median, reflecting a moderately leveraged capital structure. The company's current ratio is below one, suggesting potential liquidity tightness, though access to revolving credit facilities and cash balances mitigate immediate concerns. Deleveraging progress will be key to improving credit metrics.

overall_credit_view.text: AT&T's credit profile is supported by its scale, recurring revenue, and substantial operating cash flow, but leverage remains above the sector median and interest coverage lags peers. The indicative financial risk profile is intermediate, with limited headroom to the next leverage threshold, suggesting a stable but not strong credit standing.

Shareholder distributions absorb a significant portion of free cash flow, constraining deleveraging capacity. While the company has no commercial paper outstanding and a manageable near-term maturity profile, future refinancing needs and cost pressures warrant monitoring. The credit outlook is stable, contingent on sustained cash flow generation and prudent capital allocation.

credit_strengths.text: AT&T的營運現金流足以輕鬆覆蓋資本開支，留下可觀的自由現金流，支持償債及股東回報。公司在無線及光纖業務的規模支撐經常性收入及穩定的現金產生，營運現金流於過去三年呈上升趨勢。
營運收入強勁復甦，帶動利息覆蓋率升至行業中位數以上，為盈利波動提供穩固緩衝。通訊業務分部佔分部營運收入近乎全部，受惠於整合產品供應及共享網絡資產。

key_risks.text: AT&T的債務到期結構偏重於較後年份，但公司短期內仍面臨顯著的再融資需求。由於相當部分債務於五年後到期，再融資風險集中於未來期間，令公司暴露於利率變動及市場狀況。
網絡組件、勞工及設備成本的通脹壓力可能壓縮利潤率及現金流，而醫療及退休金成本上升可能增加福利義務。該等成本壓力，加上較高利率環境，可能對盈利能力及償債能力構成壓力。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 利息覆蓋率尚可但低於行業中位數，顯示相對同業的緩衝空間較少。自由現金流對債務比率適中，而儘管營運現金流強勁，公司償債能力取決於在競爭及成本壓力下維持當前盈利水平。
淨槓桿高於行業中位數，反映資本結構適度槓桿化。公司流動比率低於一，顯示潛在流動性緊張，儘管可動用循環信貸額度及現金結餘緩解即時憂慮。去槓桿進展將是改善信用指標的關鍵。

overall_credit_view.text: AT&T的信用狀況受其規模、經常性收入及可觀營運現金流支撐，但槓桿仍高於行業中位數，利息覆蓋率落後同業。指示性財務風險狀況為中等，距下一槓桿門檻的緩衝空間有限，顯示信用狀況穩定但不強勁。
股東分派佔自由現金流相當部分，限制去槓桿能力。儘管公司並無未償還商業票據及短期到期結構可控，未來再融資需求及成本壓力值得監察。信用展望穩定，取決於持續現金流產生及審慎資本配置。
